## The question

[What symbol is this?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/187625/what-symbol-is-this), asked by [Igor](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/56454/igor) on TeX Stack Exchange (2014-07-02; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> ![Symbol][q-1]
>
> I need the command to display this symbol in LaTeX or, at least, its name.
>
> I guess it’s from some kind of a mathematical or informatics discipline. I saw it in article called “[A comparison of collapsed Bayesian methods for probabilistic finite automata][q-2]”. Actually, I have no idea what it is all about: I just started learning LaTeX and I have to copy this article. This symbol is used just as if it is a casual letter like *x* or *y*. The line which includes it is,
>
> > Input : a(this symbol), N, BurnInTime, SamplingNum, Period
>
>
>   [q-1]: DYpgh.jpg
>   [q-2]: http://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs10994-013-5410-3#page-1
:::

To me this looks like a blackboard bold lowercase *a*.  Specifically, it looks like the lowercase *a* from the [bbold](http://luc.devroye.org/fonts-26732.html) font.  

![bbold font][1]

For blackboard bold capitals you can use the `\mathbb` macro provided by the `amsfonts` or `amssymb` packages.  But `$\mathbb{a}$` gives a backwards *G*.

Instead, you need to load the whole `bbold` font.  Here's a quick snippet to do that.  

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\DeclareSymbolFont{bbold}{U}{bbold}{m}{n}
\DeclareSymbolFontAlphabet{\mathbbold}{bbold}

\begin{document}
$\mathbbold{a}$
\end{document}
```

![bbold a][2]

See also https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/488/blackboard-bold-characters

  [2]: j9CzT.png
